item.p: The tree-sitter runtime (MIT) is vendored under third_party/tree-sitter/, pinned to a release tag.
Grammars live under grammars/<language>/grammar.js. The generated parser (and any external scanner) is committed so the build needs no Node.js; a script regenerates it with a pinned tree-sitter-cli.

sxml walks the concrete syntax tree and builds its own structures (the XML tree arena, the XPath/XQuery abstract syntax, then the shared IR). The concrete syntax tree is freed before the parse function returns.
Any ERROR or MISSING node is a static error (XML: not well-formed; XPath/XQuery: XPST0003). Error recovery never accepts input.
What a context-free grammar cannot express (XML well-formedness constraints, entity expansion, namespace processing, XQuery lexical constraints) is checked in the tree-building step.

Vendored third-party code is exempt from docs/C_GUIDELINES.md and the lint gates. The tree-sitter runtime allocates with malloc unless ts_set_allocator is called, and that hook is process-global, so sxml does not call it. This exemption is limited to the parse step.
